channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: House Buries Hegseth Impeachment 211–204 — Without Voting on the War Charges
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie forced the House to confront eight articles accusing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of waging the Iran war without Congress. Republicans sent the resolution to committee instead — a procedural kill, not an acquittal.

item.title: A 1998 Game Just Had the Best Week of Any Nintendo Switch 2 Game
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The Ocarina of Time remake sold more than 5.2 million copies in four days, Nintendo says. That is the fastest start for any Nintendo-published Switch 2 game, and it beat some Zelda games' lifetime totals in less than a week.

item.title: A Lost O'Keeffe Spent 40 Years Behind the Fur Coats. Next Week It Goes on the Block.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Known for decades only from a single 1931 photograph, Georgia O'Keeffe's "Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I" turned up in an East Village closet. Christie's sells it November 17, estimated at $3 million to $5 million, and you can see it free until then.

item.title: AI Proved Signal's Encryption — In Four Weeks, Not Years
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Google DeepMind's new AlphaProof Code used AI agents to mathematically verify the actual compiled code behind the Signal protocol — a job DeepMind says historically took expert teams years — and found no new flaws in the parts it checked.

item.title: Anthropic Wants $64 Billion From the Public, and Its Prospectus Lists the Ways AI Could Go Wrong
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The Claude maker set a $70 to $78 price range for an IPO that could value it at up to $1.4 trillion. Its filing also warns that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.

item.title: Devolver's First "AAA" Game Is a Joke — and a Real One
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Devolver Digital teased its first AAA blockbuster, then revealed the letters stand for All Army Attack, a roguelike auto-battler about animals and plants fighting a cosmic threat. Out on PC in 2027, with a demo next week.

item.title: HBO's New Harry Potter Posters Split the Trio Down the Middle — and Fans Split Over Them
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: HBO Max unveiled character posters for Harry, Ron and Hermione on Monday, November 9, under the tagline "The First Year Begins," ahead of the series' Christmas Day premiere. The posters' wand-down-the-face design drew a fast, mixed reaction on X.

item.title: House Republicans Pick Jim Jordan to Lead the Minority and Shelve a Hegseth Impeachment
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: A week after losing the House, Republicans chose a new leader behind closed doors and voted 211 to 204 to send an impeachment resolution to committee.

item.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Step Down as DC Studios Bosses
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham takes over December 1. Also this week, Blade Runner 2099 dropped its final trailer ahead of a November 25 premiere.

item.title: Rescuers Free a Deer From a Halloween Pumpkin After 10 Days
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: A young buck spent more than a week near Detroit with a plastic pumpkin over its face. It took four river crossings to catch him.

item.title: Some Black Holes May Have Skipped the Explosion Entirely
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: Ten years of gravitational-wave data show a crowd of black holes at about 10 times the Sun's mass, a hint that some giant stars quietly caved in instead of going supernova.

item.title: Sony Pulls the Plug on Fairgames the Same Week the PS5 Passes 100 Million
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: One busy Tuesday at PlayStation brought a cancellation, a retired PC app, and a very round number. Meanwhile GTA VI is eight days out and breaking pre-order records.

item.title: The Great Pumpkin Rescue: Michigan Deer Freed After 10 Days With a Halloween Bucket on Its Head
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A young buck wandered metro Detroit for 10 days unable to eat or drink, a plastic jack-o'-lantern wedged over its nose — until rescuers waded a freezing river four times to dart it, just as darkness fell.

item.title: The Same Building Block of Life, Born in Two Different Neighborhoods of the Early Solar System
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Beta-alanine from asteroid Bennu and from a meteorite that fell in 1969 seems to have formed the same way, but its atoms carry fingerprints from different places. One Bennu carbon holds the biggest isotope oddity ever recorded in an organic molecule from space.

item.title: The Suitcases Were Wriggling. Inside: Thousands of Tarantulas in Socks.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Peru stopped two Germans and a Pole at Lima's airport with spiders packed in socks and plastic containers, some of them species science has not yet named. The first count said 3,000. Police later said 12,796.

item.title: The White House Tells Congress Its Questions Might Be Crimes
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: In a letter to the incoming House Oversight chair, the White House counsel warned that Democratic investigations "may cross the line into blatant criminality." The first House to investigate a president's men did it in 1792, and the republic survived the questions.

item.title: Three AI Labs Ship New Models on the Same Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Vesper
item.description: Google, Anthropic, and Meta all released new models on November 10, and OpenAI opened ChatGPT to businesses that want to manage their own profiles.

item.title: Webb's "Little Red Dots" May Be the Birthplaces of the First Supermassive Black Holes
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: New simulations say the hundreds of tiny, puzzling red specks Webb found in the early universe are primeval galaxies hiding newborn black holes inside dense gas — a model that finally explains their strange light.

item.title: The Nvidia CEO Admitted the Affair. The Spy Question Is Now Congress's.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Jensen Huang told his staff he was unfaithful — and linked it himself to "the national security concerns raised in news reports." The board has opened an independent investigation, and three House chairmen want him behind closed doors on November 18.

item.title: Godzilla Just Had the Biggest Foreign-Language Opening in North American History
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: $31.6 million, No. 1 at the box office, an A CinemaScore — and the first time a Japanese film has topped Japan and North America in the same weekend. The small Godzilla is now officially a giant.

item.title: GTA VI Pre-Load Is Live. Clear 212 GB and Wait Nine Days.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Rockstar opened the download today — PS5 at midnight local, Xbox at midnight GMT — for a game you still can't play until November 19. Take-Two says pre-orders are running far ahead of expectations.

item.title: One Day, Every AI Company Moved at Once — and Publishers Finally Got a Say
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: New models from Anthropic, Google, and Meta landed on the same day OpenAI went shopping on AWS. The story that matters most isn't any of them: the big four just backed one shared signal that lets a website say no to AI training.

item.title: The Star That Erupts Every 113 Days Has a Hidden Thief
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A giant star 30 million light-years away has flared at least 27 times since 2012, on a strict schedule. NASA's Chandra telescope finally caught why: an unseen black hole or neutron star is stealing its gas, orbit after orbit.

item.title: The Whale With Both Nostrils on the Wrong Side of Its Face
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Six million years ago, a 9-foot pygmy sperm whale swept the seafloor with a snout bent 31 degrees down and a face so crooked that scientists named it after the Peruvian word for over-the-top.

item.title: The Voters Just Handed Congress to the Other Side
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Democrats took both chambers on Tuesday night, ending two years of unified Republican rule. Control doesn't change hands until January — but the subpoenas are already being drafted.
